# anpan

The goal of anpan is to consolidate statistical methods for strain
analysis. This includes automated filtering of metagenomic functional
profiles, testing genetic elements for association with outcomes,
phylogenetic association testing, and pathway-level random effects
models.

  

![](reference/figures/1_overview.png)

## Dependencies

anpan depends on R ≥4.1.0 and the following R packages, most of which
are available through CRAN (the exception being cmdstanr):

``` r

pkgs = c("ape", 
         "data.table",
         "dplyr", 
         "fastglm",
         "furrr", 
         "ggdendro",
         "ggnewscale",
         "ggplot2",
         "loo",
         "patchwork",
         "phylogram",
         "posterior",
         "progressr",
         "purrr",
         "R.utils",
         "remotes",
         "stringr",
         "tibble",
         "tidyselect")

install.packages(pkgs, Ncpus = 4)

install.packages("cmdstanr", 
                 repos = c("https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/", getOption("repos")))
```

If the `cmdstanr` installation doesn’t work you can find more detailed
instructions [at this link](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/).

Once you’ve installed `cmdstanr`, you will need to use it to install
CmdStan itself:

``` r
library(cmdstanr)
check_cmdstan_toolchain()
install_cmdstan(cores = 2)
```

On some servers it may also be necessary to install / load the GNU MPFR
library prior to installing CmdStan.

## Installation

Once you have the dependencies, you can install anpan from github with:

``` r
remotes::install_github("biobakery/anpan", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## Examples

The vignette has step-by-step walkthroughs and detailed documentatation
on the most important functionality.

## Example - element testing

You can filter large microbial gene profiles and look for associations
with outcomes (while controlling for covariates) with
[`anpan_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_batch.md):

``` r
library(anpan)

anpan_batch(bug_dir           = "/path/to/functional_profiles/",
            meta_file         = "/path/to/metadata.tsv",
            out_dir           = "/path/to/output",
            annotation_file   = "/path/to/annotation.tsv", #optional, used for plots
            filtering_method  = "kmeans",
            model_type        = "fastglm",
            covariates        = c("age", "gender"),
            outcome           = "crc",
            plot_ext          = "pdf",
            save_filter_stats = TRUE)
```

This will run an anpan batch analysis for each functional profile
present in `bug_dir` (there should be one input file per bug). This will
run the adaptive filtering and functional modeling for the genes in each
bug. The outputs will include the filter statistics, filter diagnostic
plots, model statistics, and results plots for each bug.

## Example - phylogenetic generalized linear mixed model

You can run a PGLMM with the
[`anpan_pglmm()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pglmm.md)
function. This type of model assesses the degree to which the
phylogenetic structure within a species associates with the outcome. It
uses integrated leave-one-out cross-validation to compare predictive
performance against the “base” GLM (without phylogenetic information).

``` r
meta_file = "/path/to/metadata.tsv" 
tree_file = "/path/to/file.tre"

anpan_pglmm(meta_file,
            tree_file,
            outcome = "response")
```

There is a corresponding
[`anpan_pglmm_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pglmm_batch.md)
function that can be pointed to a directory of tree files with the
`tree_dir` parameter.

## Example - pathway random effects model

Using pathway and species abundance profiles, you can fit a
pathway-level random effects model of the form
`log10(pwy_abd) ~ log10(species_abd) + (1 | pwy) + (0 + group | pwy)`
with
[`anpan_pwy_ranef()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pwy_ranef.md).
This assesses how well a binary `group` variable explains variation in
pathway abundance.

``` r
anpan_pwy_ranef(bug_pwy_dat,
                group_ind = "group01")
```

Detailed explanation and interpretation of all three model types can be
found in the vignette `vignette("anpan_tutorial", package = 'anpan')`.

## FAQ

> I’m having installation issues, what’s wrong?

There’s more to the installation than the `install_github()` command.
Please ensure that you’ve read the [Dependencies](#dependencies) section
fully. The relatively unusual installation steps are:

- Installing `cmdstanr` from the Stan website
- Using `cmdstanr` to install CmdStan

> I have questions, where can I get help?

You can ask on the biobakery help forum: <https://forum.biobakery.org/>

> What’s with the name?

- The name “anpan” was chosen to fit into the
  [biobakery](https://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/tools/) bread theme
  and because it’s short and easy to pronounce and remember.
- [Real
  anpan](https://duckduckgo.com/?q=anpan&t=h_&iax=images&ia=images) are
  good.
- The current frontrunner backronym is “ANalysis of microbial
  Phylogenies And geNes” (credit to Meg Short).
- Capitalization of the name follows [the xkcd
  rule](https://xkcd.com/about/). All lowercase “anpan” is preferred,
  and all uppercase “ANPAN” is acceptable in formal contexts or the
  start of a sentence, but mixed-case “Anpan” should be avoided.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`anpan()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan.md) :
  Run anpan
- [`anpan_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_batch.md)
  : Apply anpan to a many bugs
- [`anpan_pglmm()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pglmm.md)
  : Run a phylogenetic generalized linear mixed model
- [`anpan_pglmm_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pglmm_batch.md)
  : Run PGLMMs on a batch of tree files
- [`anpan_pwy_ranef()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pwy_ranef.md)
  : Estimate a species-pathway abundance random effects model
- [`anpan_pwy_ranef_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_pwy_ranef_batch.md)
  : Fit the pathway random effects model for multiple bugs
- [`anpan_repeated_measures()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_repeated_measures.md)
  : Use repeated measures to refine the gene model
- [`anpan_subjectwise_pglmm()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_subjectwise_pglmm.md)
  : Fit a subject-wise PGLMM
- [`anpan_vignette()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/anpan_vignette.md)
  : Open the anpan vignette
- [`compute_clade_effects()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/compute_clade_effects.md)
  : Compute a clade effect
- [`draw_mvnorm()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/draw_mvnorm.md)
  : Draw a sample from a multivariate normal distribution
- [`filter_batch()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/filter_batch.md)
  : Filter a batch of files
- [`filter_gf()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/filter_gf.md)
  : Filter a gene family file
- [`get_cor_mat()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/get_cor_mat.md)
  : Get the correlation matrix of a tree
- [`get_genome_intersect_counts()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/get_genome_intersect_counts.md)
  : Get genome intersection counts
- [`olap_tree_and_meta()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/olap_tree_and_meta.md)
  : Overlap a tree and metadata
- [`plot_cor_mat()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_cor_mat.md)
  : Plot a correlation matrix Generate a colorful heatmap visualization
  of a correlation matrix
- [`plot_elpd_diff()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_elpd_diff.md)
  : Plot the ELPD difference interval
- [`plot_genome_intersection_histograms()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_genome_intersection_histograms.md)
  : Intersection histograms
- [`plot_genome_intersections()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_genome_intersections.md)
  : Plot genome intersections
- [`plot_half_cor_mat()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_half_cor_mat.md)
  : Plot a rotated half correlation matrix
- [`plot_lines()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_lines.md)
  : Make a filter-labelled line plot
- [`plot_outcome_tree()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_outcome_tree.md)
  : Plot a tree file showing the outcome variable
- [`plot_p_value_histogram()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_p_value_histogram.md)
  : Make a p-value histogram
- [`plot_pwy_ranef()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_pwy_ranef.md)
  : Plot a pathway random effects result
- [`plot_pwy_ranef_intervals()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_pwy_ranef_intervals.md)
  : Plot a pathway random effects result
- [`plot_results()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_results.md)
  : Plot the data for top results
- [`plot_tree_with_post()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_tree_with_post.md)
  : Plot a tree and the PGLMM posterior on phylogenetic effects
- [`plot_tree_with_post_pred()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/plot_tree_with_post_pred.md)
  : Plot a tree and the PGLMM posterior predictive
- [`read_and_filter()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/read_and_filter.md)
  : Read and filter a gene family file
- [`read_bug()`](https://andrewghazi.github.io/anpan/reference/read_bug.md)
  : Read a bug's genefamily file
